approachQuestion.prompt: A row contains n particles, 0<=n<=100,000. Each particle is an integer in [-1,000,000,000,-1] or [1,1,000,000,000], listed left to right; absolute value is size. Positive moves right, negative left. Only opposing adjacent survivors collide. Smaller disappears; equal sizes both disappear; larger survives and may collide again. Return survivors in order. Example [5,2,-4] -> [5].

options.text: Keep surviving particles in a stack. For each incoming negative particle, resolve repeatedly against positive top: remove the smaller; remove both on equality; stop if incoming dies or no collision remains. Push the incoming particle if it survives after all such collisions; positive incoming particles are pushed directly.
options.feedback: In [8,-5,-4], -5 dies against 8, then -4 also collides with 8 and dies.

options.text: For every negative particle, compare only with its immediately preceding original input particle.
options.feedback: That particle may already be gone: in [5,2,-4], 2 disappears against -4, then -4 must collide with 5 and disappear too.

options.text: Sort by absolute size then cancel opposite signs.
options.feedback: Sorting destroys left-to-right collision order; a particle cannot collide with an arbitrary same-sized particle elsewhere in the row.

options.text: Scan particles left to right, but resolve at most one collision for each incoming negative particle.
options.feedback: For [3,2,-4], -4 destroys 2 and must then destroy 3; stopping after one collision leaves a particle that should be gone.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For ordered-particle-collisions-optimal, let n be the number of input operations or tokens. Choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: The input is immutable; returned output is excluded from auxiliary space. All stack operations and value comparisons take constant time.
The algorithm is iterative with O(1) call-stack use. The auxiliary stack may hold up to n fixed-size entries.
No hashing, recursion, or hidden array copy occurs. Any movement between stacks counts as constant time per item.

options.text: O(log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Every particle can enter and leave the survivor stack only once.
details: Every particle is pushed at most once and popped at most once; a sequence of repeated collisions consumes prior survivors rather than revisiting them. Copying the final survivors costs at most linear time. An all-positive input retains n particles in the working stack, so total time and auxiliary space are O(n).
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: All positive particles survive in the separate working stack, reaching n entries before the returned copy is made.
“O(n²) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: A repeated collision pops a previously pushed survivor or destroys the incoming particle; those consumed particles are not rescanned later.
“O(log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: The final negative particle can destroy many earlier survivors, so the final result requires the full worst-case scan.
